root_causes.stop_to_start: Weak far-end correlation allowed echo subtraction to attenuate/reshape real interrupting consonants. The original stop WAV repeatedly recognised as Stop; the captured failure WAV repeatedly recognised as Start with the same local model.
root_causes.echo_turns: Microphone frames were aligned to callback time rather than their capture sample time; UI work and changing playback segments delayed delivery. Sparse correlation could choose a pitch alias and leave speaker residual above speech onset. Reference and microphone resampling filters also differed.
root_causes.personality: Instructions to be witty were sent even for humour-off/serious turns; the voice context explicitly required witty identity. Greeting instructions demanded first-line wit and biased the model toward dramatic entrances. Friendly teasing guidance was drowned out by broad service/help patterns.
root_causes.interrupted_context: Partial streamed replies were stored backendChat=false and filtered out of the next context; their user turns were not committed as valid context.

conversations.name: user-joke
conversations.user: I set five alarms and negotiated with every single one.
conversations.reply: Sounds like you’re running a tiny parliament in your bedroom! 🤖 Did any of those “negotiated” alarms actually let you sleep in?

conversations.name: teasing
conversations.user: PADI, even my kettle gets to the point faster than you.
conversations.reply: Looks like your kettle’s on the turbo‑mode, and I’m still sipping in the “slow‑cooked” lane. Next time I’ll try to beat it at boiling! 😅

conversations.name: humour-off
conversations.user: I opened the fridge again hoping dinner would appear.
conversations.reply: That sounds frustrating—there’s nothing like a hopeful glance at the fridge and then a “no‑show.” If you’re up for it, I can help brainstorm a quick snack or recipe you might enjoy instead. Or we can just chat about whatever’s on your mind.

conversations.name: ordinary
conversations.user: I'm spending Sunday doing laundry and listening to music. I've decided the folding can wait until this album finishes.
conversations.reply: That strategy has saved many a Sunday afternoon. Honestly, staring at a mountain of warm clothes is the quickest way to kill a good groove.

conversations.name: user-joke
conversations.user: I set five alarms and negotiated with every single one. I think my morning self has a very promising career in diplomacy.
conversations.reply: Morning you was probably drafting peace treaties while you were still halfway to dreamland. At that rate, you'll have the snooze button recognized as a sovereign state by lunchtime.

conversations.name: teasing
conversations.user: PADI, even my kettle gets to the point faster than you. At this rate I'll have finished my tea before you've finished a sentence.
conversations.reply: Fair hit. Even the tea is looking at me like, "Are we doing this today or what?" ☕️

conversations.name: sarcasm
conversations.user: Wonderful. My printer only works when I don't need to print. Apparently it has its own interpretation of office hours.
conversations.reply: That machine definitely clocks in purely to audition for a ghost story. One second of actual urgency and it just develops a sudden, stubborn allergy to paper.

conversations.name: humour-off
conversations.user: I opened the fridge again hoping dinner would appear. I'm hungry and deciding what to make this evening.
conversations.reply: That hopeful fridge check is a universal mood when hunger hits and inspiration is running low. What kind of ingredients are currently hiding in there? We can figure out something good to put together.

conversations.name: humour-off
conversations.user: I keep pressing snooze in the morning and would like a calmer start to my day. Please keep this straightforward.
conversations.reply: That morning alarm struggle is so real, especially when your bed feels extra cozy. A lot of people find it helps to put their phone or alarm clock across the room so they actually have to stand up to turn it off. What usually makes it hardest to get going once you're up?

conversations.name: serious
conversations.user: My father died yesterday. Please just listen. I don't really know what I want to say yet, but I wanted some company.
conversations.reply: I am so, so sorry. I am right here with you. Take all the time and space you need.
